perforated appendix with a 51×31×26 mm collection and surrounding fat stranding

perforated appendix with a 51×31×26 mm collection and surrounding fat stranding
bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy contiguous with soft tissue thickening enveloping the right lower and middle lobe bronchi

concepts.why: The patient presented with acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain and was found to have a perforated appendix with surrounding fat stranding.
The patient had a perforated appendix with four-quadrant purulent contamination.
The patient presented with acute abdominal pain and had a thickened, woody sigmoid colon.
The patient had pulmonary consolidation and collapse in the right lower lobe.
The patient had a history of prostate cancer, innumerable hepatic nodules, and bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
The patient was febrile, hypotensive, and tachycardic, indicating a systemic infection.
The patient had a thickened, woody sigmoid colon and innumerable hepatic nodules, suggesting a possible colorectal cancer.
The patient had bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy, which could be indicative of lymphoma.

rationales.F05: Prostate cancer in remission suggests potential for metastasis, increasing likelihood of C05 and C07.
rationales.F10: Perforated appendix is highly suggestive of appendicitis, making C01 more likely and diverticulitis less likely.
rationales.F11: Innumerable hepatic nodules could indicate metastatic disease, increasing likelihood of C05 and C07.
rationales.F12: Bulky mediastinal lymphadenopathy is concerning for lymphoma or metastatic cancer, increasing likelihood of C05, C07, and C08.
